newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea mulls foreign shr holding limit expansion.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea mulls foreign shr holding limit expansion.

text.p: South Korea's finance and economy ministry is still considering raising the foreign stock owernership ceiling on the Seoul stock market earlier than planned, a senior ministry official said on Thursday.
"It's our official stance that we are still considering the issue," said Yoon Jeung-hyun, deputy minister for the financial policy division.
South Korea plans to raise the limit to 23 percent this year from 20 percent, but no date has yet been set.
Finance minister Kang Kyong-shik told reporters on Thursday: "I have not considered the matter at all."
"What Minister Kang really means is he was not informed about the matter," Yoon said. "We have not yet reported on the issue to him."

Kang announced a new economic package at a press conference in which he said the government plans to slash tax revenues and government spending this year as part of belt-tightening measures to keep inflation under control as the economy slows.

Hopes for an announcement on the ceiling sparked buying interest in late afternoon, helping the main stock index recover from a sharp plunge. The composite stock index ended 3.43 points lower at 642.86, off the day's low of 630.37.
